div.head: VI Atr Lat 9
div.ab: K. Nemo etenim pro pecunię commutatione alicuius quempiam Christianum insontem ex patria eiciat, sed nec paganorum dominio subdat: nefas igitur est, ut quos Christus sanguinis sui effusione redemit, Iudeorum uel gentilium uinculis sint inretiti.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

note.seg: Wie dieser Text, so liest þeode nur Hs. D in V Atr 2, wo die übr. Hss. leode haben: mir scheint dies zufällig gleiche Änderung durch zwei Schreiber
Like this text, only MS D in V Atr 2 reads þeode, where the other MSS have leode: this seems to me an identical alteration made by two scribes by chance
